news.summary: Babcock's agreement brings the Red White frigate programme to at least four ships, with a letter of intent for two more built locally. The first, KRI Balaputradewa, was launched by PT PAL weeks earlier.
news.title: Indonesia adds two more Arrowhead 140 frigate licences

news.summary: The UK sold the laid-up hydrographic survey ship to the Bangladesh Navy for an undisclosed sum. It will replace the 40-year-old BNS Anushandhan.
news.title: Bangladesh buys former HMS Enterprise

news.summary: The 62.7 m ship carries VL MICA, RAM, Exocet Block 3 and a 76 mm gun. Four are on order for the UAE Navy under a 2021 contract, and Kuwait has also ordered the class.
news.title: First Falaj 3 patrol vessel, Al Taf, shown at WDS 2026

news.summary: Sri Lanka's navy and air force answered a distress call and rescued 32 sailors from the Iranian warship off the south coast. Defence sources said a submarine attacked the ship; Sri Lankan officials declined to comment on the cause at the time.
news.title: Iranian frigate IRIS Dena sinks off Galle

news.summary: UMS Thalun Min, a 3,500-tonne FF-135 type, was commissioned at Yangon on 8 March. Visible fit includes C-802 launchers, a VLS for air defence missiles, a 76 mm gun and Type 730B CIWS.
news.title: Myanmar commissions its largest home-built frigate

news.summary: Chinese state media expect the 80,000-tonne catapult carrier to be fully operational during 2026. Analysts see qualifying the J-35 and KJ-600 as the main test. A nuclear carrier is under construction at Dalian.
news.title: Fujian expected to reach full readiness this year

news.summary: PNS Hangor was commissioned at Sanya with President Zardari as chief guest. It is the first of eight boats ordered in 2015, an export Type 039B derivative of about 76 m and 2,800 tonnes; the programme runs behind schedule.
news.title: Pakistan commissions first Hangor-class submarine in China

news.summary: The new submarine and the Type 054A/P frigate called at Kota Kinabalu naval base in Sabah from 8 to 11 May on passage to Pakistan.
news.title: PNS Hangor and PNS Taimur visit Kota Kinabalu

news.summary: Photos examined by imagery analysts show an unidentified SSN of about 120 m with an unusually small sail, assessed as an advanced Type 093 variant or a new design aimed at lower noise.
news.title: Images show a new Chinese nuclear attack submarine

news.summary: At trilateral talks with Japan and Australia on 26 August, Jakarta again raised buying eight of the 6,200-tonne frigates with 32 Mk 41 cells. Contract talks wait on a parallel deal for second-hand Asagiri-class destroyers.
news.title: Indonesia revives interest in Upgraded Mogami frigates

news.summary: The first Hangor-class submarine carried out its first live missile firing in the North Arabian Sea, announced on 26 September. The navy did not name the missile.
news.title: PNS Hangor fires an anti-ship cruise missile

news.summary: The former Italian carrier was commissioned on 25 September with pennant 100. Indonesia plans to use it for disaster relief with up to ten helicopters; its badge shows a Bayraktar TB3, hinting at drone operations.
news.title: Indonesia commissions ex-Garibaldi as KRI Sriwijaya

news.summary: The Zhuhai show runs 7 to 13 December and will include a dedicated maritime display of PLA Navy equipment in active service. The full list of ships and aircraft has not been published.
news.title: Airshow China 2026 adds a naval equipment area

news.summary: The biennial exercise, running since 1 September, closed in Karachi. The navy says it validated operational plans and the shift from peace to war, and included the information and cognitive domains alongside operations at sea.
news.title: Pakistan Navy completes SEASPARK-2026

news.summary: The IRGC Navy said four vessels it accused of illegal oil transfers in the northern Gulf were struck and set on fire, and three more hit mines west of the Strait of Hormuz. It warned the US of a wider response against regional bases.
news.title: IRGC Navy claims seven vessels hit around Hormuz

news.summary: The annual exercise ran from 25 to 29 October from Said bin Sultan Naval Base at Al Musanaa, testing combat readiness across a range of simulated operational scenarios.
news.title: Royal Navy of Oman begins Exercise Sea Lion 2026

news.summary: Neom, second of three follow-on corvettes ordered in 2025, was launched at San Fernando, Spain. The last ship of the batch is due in 2029.
news.title: Navantia launches Neom, seventh Avante 2200 corvette for Saudi Arabia

news.summary: Satellite imagery shows two Type 071 LPD hulls side by side at a CSSC yard on Longxue Island, Guangzhou, alongside new hulls at Hudong-Zhonghua. One Guangzhou hull could launch by around the turn of the year.
news.title: Second shipyard joins Type 071 amphibious dock production

news.summary: India is hosting Bay of Bengal states for the first BIMSTEC maritime security exercise, with tabletop drills followed by a harbour phase running to 3 November. Sri Lanka sent its largest OPV, SLNS Gajabahu.
news.title: First BIMSTEC maritime security exercise opens in the Andamans

news.summary: The PLA Navy confirmed on 30 October that the GJ-21, a navalised GJ-11, made its first catapult launch and arrested landing aboard the amphibious assault ship Sichuan during late-October sea trials. No imagery has been released.
news.title: GJ-21 stealth drone flies from Type 076 Sichuan

news.summary: US mine countermeasures ship USS Warrior arrived on 1 November for a five-day exercise with Bangladesh Navy ships, bases and naval aviation from 2 to 6 November. A US Navy P-8A is also taking part.
news.title: CARAT Bangladesh 2026 under way at Chattogram

news.summary: ADSB, part of EDGE, launched NRA Nimi-ya-Lukeni (F301) on 29 October, the second of three corvettes for Angola. The design upgrades the Baynunah class in UAE Navy service, and its electronics layout closely resembles the Falaj 3 patrol vessels.
news.title: Abu Dhabi yard launches its first locally built BR71 Mk II corvette

news.summary: The IRGC said four tankers using a route it calls prohibited were destroyed by naval mines and two other vessels were seized. The claim has not been independently confirmed.
news.title: IRGC Navy claims four tankers struck mines south of Hormuz

news.summary: Maritime Executive reports that Admiral Yuan Huazhi, former navy commander Vice Admiral Li Hanjun and East Sea Fleet commander Vice Admiral Wang Zhongcai are among the officers dismissed. Admiral Hu Zhongming, navy commander since December 2023, remains in post.
news.title: Purge reaches the PLA Navy's top admirals

events.summary: The PCG reported over 135 Chinese maritime militia vessels massed at Whitsun Reef, inside the Philippine EEZ.
events.title: More than 135 militia ships swarm Whitsun Reef

events.source: The Defense Post (citing Iranian state media)
events.summary: A smaller derivative of the Soleimani-class missile catamaran (PC313-01) joined the IRGCN at Bandar Abbas.
events.title: IRGC Navy commissions catamaran Shahid Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis

events.summary: Iran seized the tanker, previously involved in a US-Iran oil dispute, in the Gulf of Oman.
events.title: Iranian Navy seizes tanker St Nikolas off Oman

events.summary: Second of the pair of catamaran missile corvettes commissioned the same day.
events.title: IRGCN commissions Soleimani-class corvette Shahid Hassan Bagheri

events.summary: One of two catamaran missile corvettes added to the IRGC Navy fleet.
events.title: IRGCN commissions Soleimani-class corvette Shahid Sayyad Shirazi

events.summary: Navantia's final first-batch corvette for the RSNF was commissioned at Jeddah.
events.title: Fifth Avante 2200 corvette HMS Unayzah commissioned

events.summary: Iran, China and Russia held their annual trilateral naval drill near Chabahar.
events.title: Maritime Security Belt 2024 with Russia in Gulf of Oman

events.place: Gulf of Oman near Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: IRGC commandos seized the Portuguese-flagged, Israel-linked boxship near the Strait of Hormuz.
events.title: IRGC helicopter raid seizes container ship MSC Aries

events.place: Wuchang Shipbuilding, Shuangliu base, Wuhan, China
events.summary: The lead Hangor-class AIP submarine for Pakistan was floated out at Wuchang Shipbuilding's Shuangliu base.
events.title: First Hangor-class submarine launched in Wuhan

events.summary: Hanoi called the new Chinese reef-survey ship's work in its Gulf of Tonkin EEZ illegal. The ship transmits no AIS.
events.title: Vietnam protests Haiyang Dizhi 26 reef survey

events.summary: The third Damen-built offshore patrol vessel for Pakistan was commissioned at the builder's yard in Galati (date is Naval News report date).
events.title: Pakistan commissions OPV PNS Hunain in Romania

events.summary: Pakistan inducted the first Turkish-designed MILGEM corvette at Karachi around Defence Day, alongside the arrival of PNS Hunain.
events.title: PNS Babur, first Babur-class corvette, joins fleet

events.summary: Chinese law-enforcement personnel boarded a Quang Ngai fishing boat, beat ten crew with metal bars and took their catch and gear, prompting a formal protest from Hanoi.
events.title: Vietnamese fishermen beaten, catch seized near Paracels

events.summary: Malaysia pressed ahead with drilling near Luconia even though CCG ships hovered over its oil and gas projects almost continuously.
events.title: CCG keeps constant watch over Malaysian drilling

events.place: Near St Martin's Island / Naf River mouth
events.summary: Dhaka said Myanmar's navy attacked six boats near St Martin's, killing a fisherman and detaining 57; Bangladesh Coast Guard secured releases.
events.title: Myanmar navy fires on Bangladeshi fishing boats, one killed

events.summary: A CCG vessel interfered with Pertamina's seismic work and claimed Chinese jurisdiction. Bakamla and an Indonesian Navy ship shadowed it until it left.
events.title: CCG ship disrupts Pertamina survey off Natuna

events.summary: The navies' first bilateral drill ran in the Java Sea off Surabaya with Pacific Fleet ships.
events.title: Indonesia and Russia hold first naval exercise Orruda 2024

events.summary: The Navy announced a successful flight test of its indigenous ship-launched ballistic missile, SMASH.
events.title: Pakistan Navy flight-tests SMASH ship-launched ballistic missile

events.summary: The Qatar Emiri Naval Forces took delivery of the amphibious dock at Fincantieri's Muggiano yard.
events.title: Fincantieri delivers air-defence LPD Al Fulk to Qatar

events.summary: The locally built Padma-class patrol craft joined the fleet at Khulna Naval Berth.
events.title: Khulna-built patrol vessel BNS Bishkhali commissioned

events.place: Pulau Gundul, Karimun Jawa, Java Sea
events.summary: KRI R.E. Martadinata fired an MM40 Block 3 in coastal-attack mode at an islet 66.6 km away.
events.title: Indonesian frigate fires Exocet at land target

events.summary: Two unnamed anti-submarine corvettes were commissioned at the same Navy Day ceremony (two ships, names not reported).
events.title: Myanmar commissions two new ASW corvettes on Navy Day

events.summary: The largest warship built in Myanmar was launched on Navy Day at the Thanlyin naval dockyard.
events.title: Myanmar names and launches FF-135 frigate King Thalun

events.summary: The first Type 076 LHD, hull 51, was named and launched at Hudong-Zhonghua's Changxing Island yard.
events.title: China launches Type 076 catapult amphibious carrier Sichuan

events.place: Abu Dhabi Ship Building, Musaffah, Abu Dhabi

events.summary: The IRGC Navy took into service a converted container ship operating drones and helicopters.
events.title: IRGCN unveils converted drone carrier Shahid Bagheri

events.summary: Pakistan's ninth AMAN exercise drew around 60 nations, ending with an international fleet review that included Saudi warships.
events.title: AMAN-25 multinational exercise held off Karachi

events.summary: The fifth Komodo exercise in Bali drew dozens of navies including Malaysia, the US and India.
events.title: Indonesia hosts Multilateral Naval Exercise Komodo 2025

events.summary: The 62 m missile boat was commissioned during NAVDEX 2025 in Abu Dhabi (date is report date).
events.title: UAE commissions first Falaj 3 vessel Altaf at NAVDEX

events.summary: A Chinese naval task group announced live-fire drills between Australia and New Zealand, forcing airliners to divert; a second drill followed.
events.title: PLAN task group stages live fire in Tasman Sea

events.summary: Iranian state media reported joint missile and drone strikes on naval targets in the Gulf of Oman and northern Indian Ocean.

events.summary: Second domestically built Bung Karno-class corvette floated out at PT Karimun Anugrah Sejati.
events.title: Corvette KRI Bung Hatta launched at Batam

events.summary: Naval News annual review reports a further Type 055 hull possibly launched at Jiangnan in March 2025; exact day unknown.
events.title: Type 055 destroyer launched at Jiangnan (reported March)

events.summary: Iranian, Chinese and Russian warships held the five-day trilateral drill in the Gulf of Oman.
events.title: Maritime Security Belt 2025 near Chabahar

events.summary: The second of eight Hangor-class submarines was launched at the Wuchang yard in Wuhan.
events.title: Second Hangor-class submarine Shushuk launched in China

events.summary: The 12th Type 055 overall was launched at Dalian's Dagushan facility in April 2025; exact day unknown.
events.title: Dalian launches second-batch Type 055 (April)

events.summary: The Eastern Theater Command held live-fire and simulated strike drills in the East China Sea as part of a two-day exercise.
events.title: Strait Thunder-2025A live-fire drills off Taiwan

events.summary: The Romanian-built OPV, delivered by Damen in December 2024, was commissioned at Jinnah Naval Base, Ormara.
events.title: Fourth Damen OPV PNS Yamama commissioned at Ormara

events.summary: The 80 m corvette was commissioned at its Batam builder's yard.
events.title: Indonesia commissions corvette KRI Bung Hatta

events.summary: After Chinese state media showed CCG personnel unfurling a flag on the cay, Philippine personnel landed and raised their own flag to reject Beijing's claim of control.

events.summary: Lumut Naval Shipbuilding put Malaysia's second Littoral Combat Ship into the water.

events.summary: Asian Marine Services launched the replacement survey ship later commissioned as HTMS Suriya.

events.summary: The first of two ex-Italian-programme multipurpose combat ships was handed over at Muggiano.
events.title: Fincantieri delivers PPA KRI Brawijaya to Indonesia

events.summary: Hanoi's foreign ministry said Chinese survey activity on its continental shelf without consent breached Vietnamese sovereignty and jurisdiction. No ship was named.
events.title: Vietnam protests unauthorised Chinese surveys in its EEZ

events.place: Red Sea / Gulf of Aden off Yemen

events.weapon: Exocet MM40, Exocet SM39, Black Shark torpedo

events.summary: Hubei (34) was commissioned on PLA Day and assigned to the Southern Theater Command at Zhanjiang.
events.title: Fourth Type 075 LHD Hubei confirmed in service

events.summary: While chasing and water-cannoning a PCG vessel near the shoal, a CCG ship crashed into a much larger PLAN warship, and both were visibly damaged.

events.summary: The third Hangor-class boat, future PNS Mangro, was floated out in Wuhan.
events.title: Third Hangor-class submarine Mangro launched in Wuhan

events.summary: The Sustainable Power 1404 exercise, Iran's first after the June war with Israel, included cruise missile firings.
events.title: Iranian Navy fires cruise missiles in post-war drill

events.summary: A further Type 055 hull entered the water at Jiangnan in September 2025; exact day unknown.
events.title: Jiangnan launches another Type 055 (September)

events.summary: The CCG used water cannon on Philippine ships near the shoal and said they had intruded. Manila called China's account disinformation.

events.summary: The third second-batch Type 055 from Dalian was launched in October 2025; exact day unknown.
events.title: Dalian launches 14th Type 055 (October)

events.summary: The bilateral drill ran 15-23 October in Selangor and the Straits of Malacca with PLAN ships participating.

events.title: Pakistan Navy conducts new SMASH anti-ship ballistic missile test

events.title: Floating base Kurdistan joins Iranian Navy; Sahand returns

events.title: Final LMS Batch II corvette Tunku Osman Jewa launched

events.summary: A CCG cutter struck BRP Datu Magat Salamat about 54 nm off Palawan while it was handing out fuel to fishermen, damaging railings and deck fittings. No one was hurt.
events.title: CCG rams BFAR fuel-supply vessel near Sabina Shoal

events.summary: CCG ships made dangerous close-range manoeuvres and stopped a rotation and resupply mission to the Sierra Madre. It was the first publicly known obstruction since the July 2024 provisional arrangement.
events.title: China blocks Ayungin resupply, first since 2024 deal

events.summary: The newly commissioned Hangor submarine fired an anti-ship cruise missile in its first live-weapon firing, witnessed by the naval chief.
events.title: PNS/M Hangor makes maiden anti-ship missile firing

events.summary: Second ship of the 2025 batch launched at Navantia's Bay of Cadiz yards.
events.title: Seventh Avante 2200 corvette HMS Neom launched

events.summary: A BFAR fuel run to 40-50 Filipino fishing boats was completed while CCG and PLAN ships kept watch from the shoal's approaches without interfering.
events.title: CCG and PLAN shadow Philippine fuel delivery at Scarborough

events.summary: The PCG is investigating a blue-and-white Chinese ship, watched since 3 Oct, that was towing a craft carrying sensors and antennas inside the lagoon. Three CCG ships, five militia vessels and a PLAN warship were nearby.
events.title: Unidentified Chinese vessel with sensor payload inside Scarborough lagoon

last.place: Bay of Bengal, after transiting the Malacca Strait

vessels.name: Da Yang Hao
vessels.note: A deep-sea resource exploration ship carrying AUVs, active on Indian Ocean ridges and seen near Indian missile-test areas in 2025-26.
vessels.operator: China Ocean Mineral Resources R&D Association (COMRA) / Ministry of Natural Resources

sightings.text: Ran parallel survey lines along Taiwan's east coast for five days.
Came into the Bay of Bengal through the Malacca Strait, according to ThePrint (which calls it Da Yang Yi Hao).

last.place: Near Japan (revisiting Chinese seabed sensor sites)

vessels.name: Dong Fang Hong 3
vessels.note: A university research ship that Reuters found doing extensive seabed mapping near Taiwan, Guam and the approaches to the Malacca Strait.
vessels.operator: Ocean University of China

sightings.text: Serviced Chinese ocean sensors that can detect undersea objects.

sightings.place: Indian Ocean between Sri Lanka and Indonesia (Malacca approaches)
sightings.text: Ran back and forth across the western approaches to the Malacca Strait, according to ship-tracking data.

last.place: Port of Colombo, Sri Lanka

vessels.name: Hai Yang 24 Hao
vessels.note: A PLA Navy survey ship whose Colombo call was postponed over Indian concerns before going ahead in August 2023.
vessels.operator: PLA Navy

sightings.text: The Sri Lanka Navy received it in Colombo for a replenishment visit.
Local media reported the docking went ahead after a delay linked to Indian objections.

last.place: Indian Ocean Region

vessels.name: Hai Yang Di Zhi Shi Hao (Haiyang Dizhi 10)
vessels.note: A geological survey ship that has worked offshore Pakistan and that India kept out of its EEZ in 2022.
vessels.operator: Guangzhou Marine Geological Survey, China Geological Survey

sightings.text: Wrapped up a two-month joint mapping expedition with Pakistan's National Institute of Oceanography and support from the Pakistan Navy.
The Indian Navy blocked it from entering India's EEZ.

last.place: Gulf of Tonkin, Vietnam EEZ

vessels.name: Hai Yang Di Zhi 26
vessels.note: A new reef-survey ship built for South China Sea island and reef geology. It transmits no AIS, and Vietnam protested its Gulf of Tonkin work.
vessels.operator: China Geological Survey

sightings.text: Hanoi called the ship's survey in its EEZ illegal and raised it directly with Beijing's ambassador.

last.place: Malaysian EEZ off Borneo, near the West Capella drillship

vessels.name: Haiyang Dizhi 8
vessels.note: A seismic survey ship known for long survey runs inside Vietnam's EEZ near Vanguard Bank in 2019 and for shadowing Malaysian drilling in 2020.
vessels.operator: Guangzhou Marine Geological Survey, China Geological Survey

sightings.text: Vietnam's foreign ministry said the ship had left its EEZ after weeks of surveying; it came back later in August.
Finally left Vietnamese waters after more than three months of on-and-off survey work.
Moved into Malaysian and Bruneian waters near a Petronas-contracted drillship, with CCG escort.

last.place: Bering Sea / near the Aleutians (US EEZ)

vessels.name: Kexue
vessels.note: A flagship CAS research ship that has recently worked in the Arctic and North Pacific rather than the Indian Ocean.
vessels.operator: Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (Qingdao)

sightings.text: Lingered in the Bering Sea and passed through the US EEZ near the Aleutians three times.

last.place: Arabian Sea, west of the Lakshadweep Islands

vessels.name: Lan Hai 201
vessels.note: A fisheries research ship with sonar that has surveyed the northwest Indian Ocean and Arabian Sea.
vessels.operator: East China Sea Fisheries Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Fishery Sciences

sightings.text: Carried out a fisheries resource survey in the northwest Indian Ocean.
Collected sonar data west of Lakshadweep at the same time as Shi Yan 6 and Shen Hai Yi Hao were active near India.

last.place: Near the Maldives (seamount and mineral survey)

vessels.name: Shen Hai Yi Hao
vessels.note: The support ship for the Jiaolong manned submersible, which can dive past 7,000 m. Indian sources suspect it of mapping undersea cables and routes near the Maldives.
vessels.operator: National Deep Sea Center (mother ship for the Jiaolong submersible)

sightings.text: Spent March-April 2024 working near seabed-mining areas licensed to France, Poland and Russia.
Surveyed seamounts and mineral deposits near the Maldives; it was one of three Chinese survey ships near India at the same time.

last.place: Indian EEZ near Port Blair, Andaman Islands

vessels.name: Shi Yan 1
vessels.note: A SWATH research catamaran that the Indian Navy expelled from its EEZ near the Andamans in 2019.
vessels.operator: Chinese Academy of Sciences

sightings.place: Near Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
sightings.text: An Indian warship forced it out of India's EEZ after it was found operating without permission.
The expulsion was made public in December 2019, and Beijing then told its researchers to follow UNCLOS.

last.place: East Indian Ocean

vessels.name: Shi Yan 3
vessels.note: A CAS research ship that has carried out sediment and biochemical cruises in the East Indian Ocean.
vessels.operator: South China Sea Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

sightings.text: Gathered marine sediment and ran biochemical surveys from April to June 2021.

last.place: Waters near Indonesia, en route to the Indian Ocean (Malé call scheduled 24 Apr 2026)

vessels.name: Shi Yan 6
vessels.note: A geophysical research ship that has returned to the Indian Ocean every year since 2022. Indian officials link its surveys to Indian missile-test windows and submarine operating areas.
vessels.operator: South China Sea Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

sightings.text: Docked in Colombo after a delayed clearance; Sri Lanka said the stop was for replenishment only and not for research.

sightings.place: International waters south of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
sightings.text: Its presence reportedly led India to push back a missile test from 25-27 Nov to 1-3 Dec; its declared destination was Mauritius.
Sri Lanka's foreign minister said rules for foreign research ships were still being drafted; the one-year moratorium imposed in Dec 2023 lapsed in Jan 2025.

sightings.place: Near Indonesia, heading for the Indian Ocean
sightings.text: Left Guangzhou on 5 Mar 2026 for another Indian Ocean deployment after a Nov 2025-Feb 2026 survey there, with a Malé docking planned for 24 Apr.

last.place: Northwest Pacific (polymetallic nodule area survey)

vessels.name: Xiang Yang Hong 01
vessels.note: A 4,800-tonne ocean survey ship that has run repeated East and West Indian Ocean cruises. It sat off India's east coast during the March 2024 Agni-5 MIRV test.
vessels.operator: First Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources

sightings.text: Started a 74-day survey of seabed substrate and benthic life in the western Indian Ocean.

sightings.place: Between Great Nicobar Island and the Indian peninsula
sightings.text: Came through the Malacca Strait on 6 Mar and then loitered off India's east coast during the Agni-5 MIRV test window.

sightings.place: Bay of Bengal, under 260 nm from Visakhapatnam
sightings.text: Reported in international waters off Visakhapatnam, home port of India's SSBN fleet, while the test NOTAM ran from 11 to 16 Mar.

last.place: Indian Ocean Region (tracked by Indian Navy)

vessels.name: Xiang Yang Hong 03
vessels.note: A 4,500-tonne deep-water survey ship whose 2024 port calls in the Maldives became a flashpoint between New Delhi and Malé.
vessels.operator: Third Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources (Xiamen)

sightings.text: Arrived in the Maldives during a January-May south Indian Ocean deep-water survey; Malé said the call was for crew rotation and supplies.
Made a second Maldivian port call after weeks of operating around the Maldives EEZ.

sightings.place: Near Indonesia, entering the Indian Ocean
sightings.text: Left Xiamen on 3 Jul and was tracked entering the Indian Ocean, heading back toward Maldivian waters.
One of three Chinese research ships, with Zhong Shan Da Xue and Ying Wang 7, that the Indian Navy tracked in the region.

last.place: Departed on a 250-day global survey that included the Indian Ocean

vessels.name: Xiang Yang Hong 10
vessels.note: A Hangzhou-based research ship whose recorded Indian Ocean work is southwest Indian Ocean ridge surveys. No 2024-26 public sightings were found.
vessels.operator: Second Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources

sightings.text: Carried out an 18-day scientific survey in the southwest Indian Ocean in January 2016 (approximate ridge-area position).

last.place: Japan EEZ off Kubajima (Senkaku group), Okinawa Prefecture

vessels.name: Xiang Yang Hong 18
vessels.note: A mid-size MNR survey ship with past East Indian Ocean water-column surveys. It is now active in the East China Sea near the Senkakus.
vessels.operator: Ministry of Natural Resources (Institute of Oceanography)

sightings.text: Ran a survey of roughly 75-80 days in the southern East Indian Ocean.
A Japan Coast Guard patrol watched it lower a wire into the sea for about eight hours inside Japan's EEZ.

last.place: About 7 nm west of Iroquois (Rozul) Reef, Spratlys

vessels.name: Xiang Yang Hong 33
vessels.note: A submersible-capable research ship that spent spring 2026 surveying Spratly features inside the Philippine EEZ under China Coast Guard escort.
vessels.operator: Ministry of Natural Resources

sightings.text: PCG aircraft saw it putting a service boat toward the reef with CCG 5309 escorting; Manila called this unauthorised marine scientific research.

sightings.place: Second Thomas, Sabina and other Spratly features
sightings.text: Had already worked around Ayungin, Escoda and several other features after leaving China on 15 Apr.

last.place: South-eastern Indian Ocean, south of Java (AIS fix 02:38 UTC)

vessels.name: Yuan Wang 5
vessels.note: A satellite and missile tracking ship whose 2022 Hambantota visit set off a diplomatic row; it came back to the Indian Ocean in September 2025.
vessels.operator: PLA (space/satellite tracking fleet, formerly Strategic Support Force; now under the Aerospace Force)

sightings.text: Berthed at Hambantota for six days of replenishment; Colombo had first asked for the visit to be deferred after Indian objections.

sightings.place: South of Java, heading toward the Bay of Bengal
sightings.text: Tracked re-entering the Indian Ocean about 36 hours after leaving Indonesian waters, ahead of an Indian NOTAM for 24-25 Sep.
Indian media reported it back in the region just as New Delhi closed Bay of Bengal airspace for a likely missile test.
Satellite imagery of the ship circulated, and the Indian Navy said it was monitoring the vessel.

last.place: Departed a port in Jiangsu Province for Indian Ocean monitoring missions

vessels.name: Yuan Wang 6
vessels.note: A space-tracking ship that China routinely sends to the Indian Ocean to support launches. No 2025-26 sighting was found in a qualifying outlet.
vessels.operator: PLA (space/satellite tracking fleet, formerly Strategic Support Force; now under the Aerospace Force)

sightings.text: Sailed for a round of spacecraft-monitoring work in the Indian Ocean, according to Chinese state media.

last.place: Indian Ocean (entered ahead of Indian missile tests; 2023, exact date not confirmed)

vessels.name: Yuan Wang 7
vessels.note: The newest Yuan Wang ship, reported in the Indian Ocean ahead of Indian missile tests. An April 2026 entry via Indonesia was reported only by a secondary defence blog and is left out here.
vessels.operator: PLA (space/satellite tracking fleet, formerly Strategic Support Force; now under the Aerospace Force)

last.place: Indian Ocean Region

vessels.name: Zhong Shan Da Xue
vessels.note: China's largest oceanographic research ship (114 m, 6,800 t, about 100 people aboard), tracked by India in the Indian Ocean in 2024.
vessels.operator: Sun Yat-sen University

sightings.text: Satellite imagery placed it in the Indian Ocean with two other Chinese research ships while the Indian Navy tracked them.

hotspots.name: Gulf of Tonkin
hotspots.note: China drew new baselines here in 2024, and Vietnam has protested Chinese survey ships in its EEZ.

hotspots.name: Iroquois Reef (Rozul Reef), southern Reed Bank
hotspots.note: A militia swarming point close to the Reed Bank gas prospects, and a target of China's 2026 research-ship surveys.

hotspots.name: Luconia Shoals (Beting Patinggi Ali / Raja Jarom)
hotspots.note: Off Sarawak, where AMTI and RFA report CCG patrols that are nearly continuous and shadow Petronas operations.

hotspots.name: North Natuna Sea (Indonesian EEZ)
hotspots.note: Where the nine-dash line overlaps Indonesia's EEZ. CCG ships have disrupted Pertamina seismic surveys there.

hotspots.name: Paracel Islands (Hoang Sa / Xisha)
hotspots.note: Held by China since 1974. Vietnamese fishermen there are boarded, beaten and have their catch seized.

hotspots.name: Pratas Islands (Dongsha)
hotspots.note: A Taiwan-held atoll that CCG ships have entered 39+ times since Feb 2025, according to Taiwan's CGA.

hotspots.name: Reed Bank (Recto Bank)
hotspots.note: A gas-rich bank inside the Philippine EEZ, where survey and drilling ships have been harassed.

hotspots.name: Sabina Shoal (Escoda / Xianbin Jiao)
hotspots.note: Lies about 75 nm off Palawan on the route to Second Thomas, and has seen rammings and a radar lock-on.

hotspots.name: Sandy Cay (Pag-asa Cays / Tiexian Jiao)
hotspots.note: Sandbars just off Thitu that both China and the Philippines landed on in April 2025 to plant flags.

hotspots.name: Scarborough Shoal (Bajo de Masinloc / Huangyan Dao)
hotspots.note: Under China's effective control since 2012. Beijing declared a nature reserve there in Sep 2025, and CCG, militia and PLAN ships are now present year-round.

hotspots.name: Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin / Ren'ai Jiao)
hotspots.note: Site of the grounded BRP Sierra Madre outpost. Resupply runs face repeated CCG interference, and a July 2024 provisional deal broke down in 2026.

hotspots.name: Thitu / Pag-asa Island (Zhongye Dao)
hotspots.note: The Philippines' main Spratly settlement, ringed almost permanently by militia ships and CCG cutters.

hotspots.name: Vanguard Bank (Bai Tu Chinh / Wan'an Tan)
hotspots.note: Vietnamese oil and gas blocks where CCG ships and the Haiyang Dizhi 8 survey ship operated.

hotspots.name: Whitsun Reef (Julian Felipe / Niu'e Jiao)
hotspots.note: A regular anchorage for large militia flotillas, with 200+ vessels in 2021 and 135+ in Dec 2023.

notes.text: First catapult launch and arrested recovery at sea, aboard Type 076 Sichuan.
First of class Al Taf displayed at World Defense Show 2026.
Sale of ex-HMS Enterprise to Bangladesh agreed; replaces BNS Anushandhan.
State media expect full operational readiness during 2026.
GJ-21 stealth UCAV made first catapult launch and arrested landing aboard Sichuan during sea trials.
Imagery shows two new Type 071 hulls building at Guangzhou in addition to new hulls at Hudong-Zhonghua, pointing to at least five more ships for the class.
Images of an apparently new ~120 m SSN with a very small sail; possibly an advanced 093 variant.
Commissioned as KRI Sriwijaya (100); disaster-relief role with up to ten helicopters.
Two more Arrowhead 140 design licences agreed with Babcock; programme now at least four ships.
IRIS Dena sank off Galle, Sri Lanka; the Sri Lanka Navy rescued 32 sailors.
IRGCN claimed four vessels struck in the northern Gulf and three mined west of Hormuz.
IRGC claimed four tankers were destroyed by its mines south of Hormuz and two vessels seized; not independently confirmed.
SLNS Gajabahu sailed from Colombo for India to take part in the first BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise (30 Oct-3 Nov).
UMS Thalun Min commissioned at Yangon.
PNS Hangor commissioned at Sanya, China; first of eight boats.
First live firing of an anti-ship cruise missile in the North Arabian Sea.
Seventh Saudi Avante 2200 corvette, Neom, launched at San Fernando; follow-on batch of three to complete by 2029.

briefs.author: Dr Lee Willett
briefs.summary: Unauthorised drones over French Navy exercise sites near Toulon prompted an investigation. NATO's naval armaments group is prioritising counter-UAS, citing one-way drone attacks on ships in the Gulf and Red Sea that can drain a warship's interceptor stocks.
briefs.title: Drone sightings at Toulon sharpen NATO's naval counter-drone push

briefs.summary: A new Thales facility near Sydney will build and sustain towed-array and other sonars for Australia's Hunter-class frigates, Collins submarines and uncrewed craft. The article frames high-end ASW against the PLA Navy's growing submarine force as central to Indo-Pacific deterrence.
briefs.title: Thales opens Sydney sonar plant aimed at PLAN submarine threat

briefs.author: Dr Thomas Withington
briefs.summary: Stratus-RS is a ramjet anti-radiation missile that finds enemy radars with synthetic aperture radar and satellite navigation rather than a passive RF seeker. France and the UK lead development talks; launch from warship vertical cells is under consideration.
briefs.title: MBDA's Stratus-RS radar-hunting missile could go to sea

briefs.author: Dr Thomas Withington
briefs.summary: Babcock's Nomad runs on tablets and phones to clean, transcribe, translate and analyse captured voice and data traffic, easing the need for linguists forward. The UK MOD bought it as an urgent operational requirement.
briefs.title: UK fields AI tool to process intercepted communications

briefs.author: Dr Thomas Withington
briefs.summary: France's procurement agency is working with Thales and Lacroix on Dauphin, an off-board active decoy carried by a UAV that uses DRFM jamming to spoof X-band anti-ship missile seekers. Flight trials are expected around 2027, with Red Sea missile attacks on Western warships cited as the driver.
briefs.title: France develops drone-borne decoy to pull missiles off warships

briefs.summary: At Euronaval 2026 the Italian firm displayed its Adrian drone-warfare system, a naval jammer, a triple-band laser DIRCM and an EMSO command tool that fuses the electromagnetic picture. Adrian already sails on front-line Italian Navy ships.
briefs.title: ELT Group shows naval jammer, DIRCM and counter-drone suite
